items.title: HoYo 的合作怪物杀手 Nodusfall 的所有关键细节
items.summary: Paimon could never.

content.v: Nodusfall may look like developer miHoYo has slapped an Elden Ring-colored paint job onto Monster Hunter, but there's some signature HoYo innovation to find in between all those beastly battles and dark fantasy landscapes in its reveal trailer.

While there aren't an awful lot of specifics about the game right now, I've scraped together every gameplay clip and interview available to help explain what HoYo's breakup with anime girls is all about. From betas, to gacha, to gameplay and story, here's everything we know about Nodusfall so far.
Nodusfall release date speculation
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ZvTRQgApsSq669wkVSf6iF.jpg
Nodusfall release date details and speculation

Nodusfall doesn't have a solid release date yet—it doesn't even have a release year. That's typical for a HoYo game, though. It doesn't tend to announce release dates until a game's final round of beta testing is coming up.

Even though there's no release window HoYo's ever-reliable pattern of three open betas before release lets us predict that Nodusfall will launch sometime in 2028. Especially as its next game, Petit Planet, is out this winter, and Honkai: Nexus Anima seems set for a 2027 release, having just finished its second open beta.

The only thing that might throw a spanner in the works is that Nodusfall isn't your typical character/critter collector that HoYo is known for. So it might not be so typical when it comes to beta testing either.
Nodusfall beta and pre-registration

Speaking of betas, you can visit the official Nodusfall site and do a two-for-one combo by pre-registering and then answering a questionnaire for possible beta selection right after. The site mentions that this is for future betas, not for one ongoing right now. So you won't be fighting those Nodusfall bosses just yet no matter how furiously fast you refresh your inbox.
Nodusfall trailers

If you want a refresh on its gorgeous dark fantasy visuals and otherworldly boss designs that'd make Elden Ring and Diablo blush, here's the reveal trailer above. There's not much gameplay here, but what there is definitely throws up inevitable comparisons to co-op combat seen in the Monster Hunter series.
Nodusfall story and setting
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/myxEcLDGu2ZNVk7gNwLtmF.jpg

The story of Nodusfall unfolds across a dark fantasy "mythic continent" teeming with corrupted legendary creatures, whose designs take inspiration from both Eastern and Western mythology. Like manticores, dragons, and giant bears. You take on the role of a "Weaver," a being "enlightened by the divine" and entrusted with sacred missions to restore order to the continent corrupted by the "Dreadnodi". So basically, you're a big important badass with divine magic powers and chunky weapons whose mission is to blast scary monsters to get new gear save the world.

On your way to annihilating ethereal beasts and untold horrors, you'll journey through distinct regions with landscapes and cultures that take equal inspiration from various real-life cultures and mythologies, with more regions set to launch post-release. My fellow Genshin Impact players will be familiar with this formula.

Thanks to its reveal trailer, we know that some of Nodusfall's landscapes include golden hills, fiery skies, dreary moors, misty forests, dusty deserts, and gargantuan canyons. So far so Elden Ring, but it sounds like there's more variety in the works.

What I'm most interested in seeing is just how dark Nodusfall ends up being. The reveal trailer suggested a mature story, which isn't a first for HoYo—Genshin has dropped its fair share of dark lore and ran—but not shifting to a wisecrack or bonkers anime moment right after would be new.
Nodusfall gameplay

Breaking from the single-player teambuilding mold that HoYo is known for, Nodusfall is actually a free-to-play co-op action game that pits you and your squad against mythical creatures. Pick a character, build a loadout, and work with up to three other players to defeat difficult bosses and get the resources needed to unlock new skills and forge new weapons.
Why yes, it is eyebrow-raisingly similar to Monster Hunter, but there are some key differences. Such as:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2mpVcLf9KmbMNZYXEq8UkF.jpg

And although not expanded on, Nodusfall's official site claims that you can "switch roles and loadouts at will". Which presumably means you're not locked to playing just one character or build per account.

In practice, judging from hands-on impressions and what little gameplay there is right now, Nodusfall looks like it's actually a mix of Elden Ring, an MMO, and Monster Hunter—not just a Monster Hunter wannabe. Yeah, this may just sound like even more games that Nodusfall is riffing on, but if there's one thing I've learned about playing HoYo games over the years it's that you should never doubt its ability to innovate on the familiar and create one heck of a satisfying combat loop.
We played Nodusfall

PC Gamer's Fraser Brown played Nodusfall right after its reveal and was pretty impressed, even as a HoYo skeptic. "First of all: Nodusfall is not remotely a soulslike," Fraser says in his Nodusfall preview . "Monster Hunter is a closer relative. Solo adventurers and groups can select contracts, and then go out into the world to hunt down big beasties. These are lengthy, elaborate fights with multiple phases, taking place in spacious outdoor areas."

"I became rather fond of the clash mechanic, where you charge up a strong attack, and release it right as the monster is about to hit you, countering the attack. It helps that I looked stylish doing it, with my already massive sword growing, transforming into a magical, glowing WMD."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/pWPUfoebFs7xRf6fpgUtfX.jpg
Is Nodusfall gacha?

There is no character gacha in Nodusfall , which means you'll never have to rely on luck (or piles of cash) to get new characters—they're all obtained by simply playing the story. No official line on if anything else will be linked to gacha systems, but HoYo has stated that cosmetic monetization is "an important avenue" that it'll be considering for Nodusfall.

So no, Nodusfall is not a gacha game in the traditional sense , but it may end up incorporating some RNG pulls elsewhere. Maybe for exclusive cosmetics similar to Where Winds Meet, or maybe even some special type of gear. Or maybe we'll get the biggest win of all and Nodusfall will be entirely gacha-free! (Please let me dream.)

items.title: 《漫长的黑暗》将再次获得新的 DLC，因为工作室将开发人员从续集转移到“不确定”的行业中生存：“我们必须适应这一点”
items.summary: Blackfrost's early access release won't make it this year after all.

content.v: Survival game The Long Dark was supposed to be over when its final story episode was released earlier this year . Developer Hinterland announced its sequel, Blackfrost , two years ago and planned to go the early access route with it just like the first game.

According to a new update from the studio, however, those plans have changed a little bit. While it continues to work on Blackfrost in the background, a small team of developers have been moved back onto The Long Dark to make new DLC for its survival mode. Hinterland hopes going back to the 9-year-old game will help it endure an "uncertain" industry.

"When we first announced Blackfrost, the sequel to The Long Dark, the game industry was in a very different place," it said. "In the short time since, entire business models have been thrown into chaos, the geopolitical situation has become extremely complicated, the picture of what the next generation of console hardware will be has become a lot less clear, and the amount of time and money players spend on new games has declined as everyone turns to the comfort and security of games they already know."

Over the next two years, the studio plans to continue updating the survival sandbox mode in the game with bug fixes, quality-of-life improvements, new features, and new regions from the final story episode. It's also going to release new DLC, one of which will come out piecemeal like its previous Tales From The Far Territory expansion pass. The second DLC "will be… different from that," it said, withholding info because it's still early in development.

Hinterland assured everyone Blackfrost is still in the works but said that its early access launch has been pushed to next year. The studio remains independent despite having publishers reach out to help with the sequel. "We've not yet encountered a partner who we feel is truly motivated by what's best for Hinterland or for our players, so we'll continue to self-fund and self-publish the game."

Hinterland said it's considering raising the price of the standalone Survival Mode as well as the new DLCs to help offset the loss from people buying them on sale. "We’re also mindful that the economic reality faced by a ton of folks today is that prices are increasing everywhere and you probably can’t really afford for games to get more expensive as well," it said. "We’re really trying to find a good balance here." Given the flood of layoffs across the games industry in the last few years and the cost of hardware skyrocketing , I can see why an indie studio like Hinterland would go back to what works as people are forced to be more picky than ever about what they spend money on. It's already hard enough making a splash on the crowded pages of Steam when you release a new game. I just hope it works out and it can continue to make the sort of things it wants to without feeling anchored to its breakout release.

items.title: 被 Steam 宠坏的现代玩家永远不会理解 MegaPak 的乐趣
items.summary: A requiem for the early days of budget PC gaming.

content.v: Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Ted, and Rick have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of Thief's Garrett or that time someone in the Vatican pirated Football Manager .

It's easy to be cynical about the modern games industry, what with developers being laid off left and right and hardware prices skyrocketing thanks to AI datacentres gobbling up all the components. But it's also worth pointing out the positives too. For starters, games are more abundant than ever before. More games get released in a single day than most people could feasibly play in an entire year, and those games cover every genre and experience imaginable. If you can think of a game you want to play, it probably exists in some form. If it doesn't, someone is probably trying to make it.

As well as being omnipresent, games are cheaper than they've ever been too. This statement might seem spurious in the era of £70 games. But aside from the fact that, relative to inflation, games are technically cheaper than they were thirty years ago, it doesn't account for the endless stream of bundles and giveaways across all digital platforms. They're so frequent that, by the time you've finished playing your current game, there's a good chance you'll be able to grab what you want to play next on some form of discount.

In short, we're spoiled for choice in a way that's drastically different from how the gaming scene was thirty years ago, when games were significantly less numerous and generally less accessible financially. It's hard to estimate because everybody's experience varies. But I think, in 1996, if you were buying a new game every month, you would have been considered to be doing pretty well. For most people, new games would have been limited to Christmases and birthdays, and a lot of people would have experienced games through shareware demos or hooky copies burned onto a CD by your mate.

I don't want to turn this article into a Facebook post by your grandad, so let's stress that even if the number of game releases was far fewer, it didn't feel like that. Still, the idea of being able to hoover up a whole bunch of PC games for pennies was virtually unthinkable.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xMyxZh3evw4FgBhBtnpYrK.jpg

There was one big exception though—the MegaPak. The MegaPak was the closest thing we had to Humble Bundle (without the charity element), a big-box compilation of games that had typically been released one or two years prior. The MegPak was the production of Megamedia Corp, which has relatively little footprint online. But I can tell you that its handful of other publishing credentials include the Ukrainian Quake clone Chasm: The Rift .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ePfEGFZT576Mwxi8zVKqLV.jpg

The first Megapak was released in 1994, featuring eleven games. You can tell this because the box proudly displays the number 11 in massive yellow font, which I suppose indicates how novel the concept was. It has also led some database sites to label it as "Megapak 11", which was incredibly confusing for me when researching for this article because the Megapak line ended at number 10.

Nonetheless, it was probably right for Megapak to focus on the number of games for marketing purposes, because the quality of the titles in the pack is, shall we say, variable? The highlights of the first Megapak are Ultima spinoff World of Ultima: The Savage Empire, combat flight sim F-14 Tomcat, and Test Drive 3: The Passion—a title that makes it sound like a vehicular reimagining of Christ's crucifixion. Also included was Dinosaur Safari, an edu-tainment game that was halfway between an adventure game and Microsoft Encarta. I bring this up for no reason other than I played a ton of it on my dad's PC—Megapak notwithstanding.

This is a typical overview of the content of a Megapak, a lesser title from a big franchise, a bunch of fair to middling vehicle simulators, and a couple of oddball picks thrown in. As time went on, juicier games began to appear. Megapak 2 included Ocean's Jurassic Park, which people fondly remember today. Megapak 3, meanwhile, had TFX, a jet-fighting sim that was a cut above most combat sims of the era.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/JcxTUU98X9EbfBhW7e9T3Q.jpg

The heyday of the Megapak came in 1996, when Megapak 5 arrived. Among the pinball game and pool simulators were several genuine PC gaming heavyweights. Most notable was Jagged Alliance, the mercenary turn-based tactics games which alongside X-COM helped formalise the genre. Also included was Apogee's Descent rival Terminal Velocity , and Looking Glass' Flight Unlimited, a well-regarded flight sim which has been somewhat forgotten in the wake of games like Thief and System Shock 2 .
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/i4QMiiM8z7XDS7JT9t7D6.jpg

These weren't the best games that would eventually feature on a Megapak. Megapak 7 has Caesar 2 and Heroes of Might and Magic, while Megapak 8 treated players to SimCity 2000 and Mechwarrior II. But Megapak 5 was the best expression of what a Megapak was meant to be, a snapshot of PC gaming in the present moment.

Megapak 5 was also the first of them I personally owned, gifted as a Christmas present in 1997. The main thing I remember about it, outside of the games themselves, is the weight of the box. Each game came on its own CD in a paper sleeve, and if I remember rightly, the pack had a bespoke manual thick enough to kill a large insect or small rodent. You could feel the value of it in your hands.

The grab-bag nature of it was also part of the appeal. I was too young to have much foreknowledge of which games in the box were worth my time and which weren't, so there was an element of discovery in playing them. It was through Megapak 5 that I discovered Entomorph: Plague of the Darkfall , which was my introduction to roleplaying games and has been lodged in my head ever since.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/S4rMxADikLATLb4MMvHLGU.jpg

The Megapak era burned bright and faded quickly, with nine volumes released between 1994 and 1998. What happened to Megapak Corp afterwards isn't entirely clear. A tenth and final Megapak collection appeared in 2001. But it was published by Empire Interactive rather than Megamedia Corp. All the games featured on this Megapak were also Empire-published titles.

Clearly then, the Megapak license transitioned from Megamedia Corp to Empire in some fashion. Unfortunately, I couldn't find any information online to confirm this, and there seems to be no mention of the Megapak name or Megamedia Corp in Empire's published accounts.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/hUpbi3g6GL9d7xBU8fNvag.jpg

Either way, there is a clear indication of why the Megapak line came to an end. In 2000, Empire launched Xplosiv, its own range of budget titles, which, alongside Sold Out, became one of the two main brands you'd find piling up in the bargain bin of UK game stores nationwide. Hence the likely scenarios are that Empire bought Megapak to kill the competition, opted not to continue with the series after a poor performance from Megapak 10, or entered into a publishing agreement with Megamedia Corp for Megapak 10 while spinning up its own budget range on the sly.

Whatever happened, the upshot was that the era of big-box PC compilations ended, and the era of lurid orange DVD cases began. I don't begrudge that—I had plenty of fun with those later budget lines too. Nor would I choose to go back to the Megapak era over our modern age of abundant, easily accessible games.

items.title: Fibbage纸牌游戏评论

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/28/fibbage-thumb-1787947104062.jpg
如果您在 2010 年代中期参加聚会，那么您很有可能至少在其中一些聚会中参加了由 Jackbox Games 背后的人员开发的聚会游戏“Fibbage”。自 2014 年第一款游戏发布以来，这款数字派对游戏在过去的 12 年里经历了多次迭代，现在 Jackbox Games 正在切断线缆，将这款主流派对游戏带到桌面上，推出适合您的棋盘游戏之夜的卡牌版本。

有助于制作这款数字虚张声势游戏的所有规则都已延续到这款新纸牌游戏中。与其他迭代一样，在《Fibbage》中，其中一名玩家将充当“揭秘者”，他将抽一张牌并大声朗读提示，其中一部分被空白，然后由其他玩家写下一个合理的选项来完成提示。然而，提出提示的人将会得到正确答案，并将其写下来并添加为正确答案。玩家们都会输入他们的答案，这些答案将被打乱，然后是一个投票期，你可以投票选出你认为正确的答案。从那里开始，根据您是否猜对以及其他人是否投票支持您的提交来获得积分，并且在您决定的无论多少轮（默认情况下为六轮）结束时得分最高的人获胜。
盒子的大小与标准精装书差不多，里面有单面纸（另一面是 Jackbox Party Pack 4 的广告）、纸板投票/积分代币（但奇怪的是没有袋子可以放进去）、六块带木板的干擦记号笔和 300 张带有提示的卡片。这些提示本身涵盖了一系列不拘一格的主题，从询问用吹风机烹饪鸭子的厨师到百事可乐的日本独有口味。令人印象深刻的卡牌数量意味着您将需要完成大量游戏才能开始多次重复，这很棒。
Fibbage Card Game，就像数字版本一样，已经成熟了，可以一次又一次地扩展，并且了解 Jackbox，我想用不了多久我们就会开始看到额外的提示卡包、不同主题的提示以及额外的标记和书写板。只要你有东西可以写，有东西可以记录分数，你就没有任何理由不能将玩家数量扩展到你想要的数量。
《Fibbage》的一切都相当成功地跳转到了实体游戏，只有一个小小的例外——写答案部分。有效吗？当然。问题是，考虑到揭露者知道答案，除非你们的小组有非常相似的笔迹，或者至少写了相似的方框字母（游戏建议你使用），否则不久你可能会开始识别玩家的笔迹。尤其是在玩家人数较少的游戏中。我遇到的一个情况。
https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/28/fibbage-2-1787946651985.jpg
我想出的一个自制魔法是，我让揭露者收集提交的内容，然后在另一张纸上抄下所有答案，然后小组对该列表进行投票。它确实增加了一个额外的步骤和更多的时间，但这确实设法使选票与答案挂钩，而不是每个人都假装自己是法医文件审查员（我查了一下；FDE 查看并比较法院的笔迹和签名 - 也可能是也可能不是其中一张卡片上的问题）。
不管你怎么玩，《Fibbage》都是我最喜欢的纯派对游戏之一。这是一款即使是老奶奶和爷爷也能玩得开心的游戏。我一直很欣赏《Fibbage》对玩家的要求更高，要求你更加聪明和有创造力，而不是过分依赖“谁的反应最有趣”来得分。我发现《反人类纸牌》和其他游戏往往会陷入这种结果。 Fibbage 的物理版本是对一款游戏的忠实改编，该游戏在派对上广受好评，我可以看到自己经常推出这款游戏。

items.title: 我希望 MMO 再次浪费我们的时间
items.summary: I've accomplished very little on a Star Wars Galaxies private server, and I wouldn't want it any other way.

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/PgGhmt5pTtxusaQQX3dHPF.png

This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice. Like our own Lincoln Carpenter, who's been enjoying a version of the galaxy far, far away from a long time ago.

After completing the initial tutorial on a private server for Star Wars Galaxies—the Star Wars-themed MMO that launched in 2003, was updated until 2005, and was shuttered in 2011—I was dumped out of a shuttle in Mos Eisley and into a warzone. Squads of rebel and imperial players were exchanging blaster fire and lobbing thermal detonators. When I asked the passing combatants why Tatooine was worth fighting over, a man in stormtrooper armor said I was lucky I wasn't PvP-flagged.

Despite the early-2000s assets and stiff animations, it was the most dynamic that an MMO had felt for me in years. But in the week I've spent revisiting Star Wars Galaxies, I've seen very little other excitement. I've killed no impressive enemies. I've done barely any quests. It's an MMO that's content to let me log in and do little of note whatsoever—and that's exactly what I've been missing.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/VdqTxaQMvu4KtxULVHxuD.png

In comparison, whenever the WoW itch gets strong enough for me to reup my subscription, I end up doing nothing but doing. Logging into WoW in 2026 means enduring a bombardment of refreshed weekly prompts and directives urging me to get on my flying mount and accelerate at breakneck speed towards whatever prescribed activity with prerequisite player count will provide my next predictable gear score increase.
A more civilized age

WoW has become a relentlessly efficient machine, ensuring players waste the least possible time while being propelled through seasonal ranks and escalating difficulty tiers. In terms of providing their users with those quantifiable successes, it's hard to argue that the MMOs of today aren't better designed than their older iterations. And yet, it's the moments when I step off the treadmill where they still feel the most magical.

When I can still find joy in WoW, it's not through the weekly content blitz. It's when I take the scenic route through an old leveling zone, and wonder what quest that dwarf running in the distance is doing. It's when I earn a grateful emote from a player of the opposite faction who can't otherwise thank me for helping them with a dicey fight. It's during the pinnacle of incidental MMO encounters: Receiving a sorely needed heal from a passing player who could've just as easily left me to die.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/STVfCeSkS5by4a2qdJsvX7.png

It's in those moments where it feels like the MMO rediscovers itself—where it recaptures the ways that multiplayer in a shared, persistent world can be a source of wonder, and not just a rote feature of the form. It's that wonder that motivated Star Wars Galaxies in 2003, and it's what its private server maintainers have worked to keep in suspended animation ever since.
Outer Rim living

My hours in Galaxies have been aimless ones. I've been casually puttering across the Tatooine wastelands, learning how to survey for minerals and water, how to harvest womp rat corpses for bones and how to use them to flavor what must be the world's worst tea—slowly gaining an understanding of its skill systems and crafting mechanics, but having no real idea whether I'm accomplishing anything another player would consider worthwhile.

I haven't used my blaster on anything more threatening than a nameless smuggler, and I'm not sure where I'd get a better shooting iron even if I wanted one. I could be answering the call to adventure as one of the galaxy's heroes, but the game's been content to let me ignore it.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/dX5Lv79Nrn6u4f9ZeDFE9C.png

And I've been content to go on ignoring. Because all that time I'm wasting out in the sands is time I've spent watching a bounty hunter tear by on a speeder bike and wondering what grim business he's on, or exchanging greetings with a Zabrak who's working on his carbine marksmanship. The hour I spent surveying eahiate iron deposits was one that led me through a sprawling, player-made city out in the dunes, its vacant tents and droid stalls and derelict cruisers parked in hand-built plazas proof that other players once shared that same space.

When I drift back through Mos Eisley, its scant environmental details and featureless wall textures feel vibrant, because the aliens, smugglers, and imperial agents I'll bump elbows with want nothing more than the pleasure of lingering there together.
Star Wars Galaxies has been dead for years—but it's a dead game that still remembers how to feel like a living world better than the market-leading MMOs that survived it.
